newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU backs aid to Albania with conditions.
newsitem.headline: EU backs aid to Albania with conditions.

text.p: The European Union has offered Albania help to get its economy and financial institutions in order, but only if Tirana works closely with the International Monetary Fund and other world bodies.
In a statement released on Tuesday, foreign ministers from the 15-nation bloc backed moves by the European Commission to give money and technical assistance to Albania.
It said that the ministers -- who met in Brussels on Monday -- had broadly endorsed Commission plans to offer aid to Albania through PHARE, the EU's main aid programme for eastern Europe.
Help would be specifically targeted at agriculture, small and medium-sized businesses and local communities, the statement said.
Technical assistance was also on offer for Albania's banking sector.
But the ministers made clear they expected Albania to stick to democratic principles. Referring to the current unrest, they called on all parties in the country to pull Albania back from crisis.
Underlining their concern, the ministers said they would bring their views to the attention of both the Albanian government and to the opposition.

In what diplomats said was a move towards putting conditions on aid, the ministers said they wanted to hear from the Albanian authorities about the Commission's offer of technical assistance in the banking sector.
"(We) invited them to cooperate with international financial institutions, notably the IMF," the ministers said.
